exos.piste: The 6-8 pairs in R6C6 and R6C8 are an engine. A 6 in R2C6 flips R6C6 to 8 and R6C8 to 6; box 3's 6 had only two places, R2C7 (row 2) and R3C8 (column 8).
Two engines at once: the 6-8 trio (R4C4, R6C6, R6C8) and the 7-8 pair in R1C1. Row 3's 6 had three places (fragile): two are cleared by the trio's 6s, the third is filled by row 3's 7.
Row 9's underlined 1 (R9C8/R9C9). A 2 in R9C9 goes up column 9 to row 4's underlined 2 (R4C8), which flips the 1-2 pair in R1C8 to 1 and clears R9C8.
Row 9's 7 had four places: R7C2 takes two of them at once through box 7. Box 1's 7 then goes to R1C1, row 3's 7 to R3C5, and a 1 fills R9C9.
An 8 in R1C6 flips two engines at once: the 7-8 pair in R1C1 (row 1) and the 6-8 pair in R6C6 (column 6). Row 7's 7 then loses its four places through column 1, column 7 and box 8.

Same engine as moves 2 and 4 (the 7-8 pair in R1C1), reached through column 1. Column 5's 6 had four places: two are filled (a 7 in R3C5, row 8's underlined 4 in R8C5), the 6s sliding through column 1 clear the other two.
Row 8's underlined 4 (R8C1/R8C5): any other digit in R8C5 sends the 4 to R8C1. Row 3's 7 had three places (fragile): R8C5 clears R3C5 through column 5, and the 4s and 9s fill the two others.
The 7-9 pair in R6C7: a 7 in R7C7 flips it to 9, then the 7s and 9s run through row 1 and column 6 down to the 6-8 trio. Aim at R5C9 (4-8-9): R6C7, R6C8 and R2C9 take one candidate each.

Other side of the 7-9 pair in R6C7: test both sides of an engine. Same target as move 8, R5C9 (4-8-9): it loses its 9 at once in box 6; the 8 and the 4 arrive through the long loop of row 1 and box 2.
Row 4's underlined 2 (R4C8/R4C9): attack both cells through their columns. A 2 in R8C9 clears R4C9; column 9's underlined 7 and row 9's 1 then flip the 1-2 pair in R1C8 to 2, which clears R4C8.
The 1-2 pair in R1C8: a 2 in R1C7 flips it to 1, and the 1s and 7s spread through rows 1 and 9 and box 8. Aim at R3C4 (2-6-8): box 2 gets an 8 (R1C5) and a 6 (R2C5), column 4 gets a 2 (R8C4).
Same arrival as move 7 (row 3's 7, three places). R7C5 holds box 8's underlined 4: a 4 there flips row 7's underlined 1 to R7C6 and drives the 7s and 4s up column 1.

Column 9's underlined 2 (R3C9/R4C9): a 2 in R3C9 flips the 2-8 pair in R4C9, which sets the 6-8 trio. Row 8's 8 had three places: columns 6 and 9 clear two, and the 2s of rows 1 and 9 fill R8C4 with a 3.
Aim at R3C9 (4-8-9): one step per candidate. A 4 in R5C9 sends box 6's 9 to R5C7, which flips the 8-9 pair in R1C7 to 8; box 3's 4 then goes to R3C8, and box 1's 4 and 9 follow.
Row 3's underlined 9 (R3C3/R3C9). Another digit in R3C3 leaves R1C1 with its 8, which flips the 8-9 pair in R1C7 to 9 and clears R3C9: two pairs falling in a row.
Row 1 does all the work: aim at R1C6 (1-7-9). An 8 in R3C9 fills row 1 with a 1 (R1C8), a 9 (R1C7) and a 7 (R1C1), each one through a pair.

Column 1's 8 had four places, and R7C1 takes one itself. A 4 there sends box 1's 4 to R3C2, which flips the 4-9 pair in R3C9; its 9 flips the 8-9 pairs in R1C7 and R5C9, whose 8s clear column 1 through rows 1 and 5.
The 3-8 pair in R7C7: a 3 in column 7 flips it to 8. Column 1's 7 had three places (fragile): R7C1 gets the 3, and the 7s of rows 8 and 1 clear the other two.
The 6-8 trio again: a 6 in R3C4 sets R4C4=8 and R6C6=6. Column 8's underlined 6 (R3C8/R6C8) is then hit on both sides, through rows 3 and 6.
Pairs falling like dominoes: 6-8 in R3C8, 6-8 in R6C8, then the 7-8 pairs of column 1 and box 7 down to R4C3. Box 5's 8 is left with R4C4 and R6C6, cleared through rows 4 and 6.
